mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, which reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200k per month signals strong labor market demand, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200.0 in the most recent month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in less than 55% of instances when PAYEMS > 200.0, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in residential investment (HOUST) combined with rising consumer confidence (RSAFS) indicates a shift from housing to non-housing consumption, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 5% in 3 months AND RSAFS increases > 2% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in interaction-triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05), or the joint signal fails to outperform baseline in 3-year rolling Rank IC tests (IC < 0.04).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index 2017=100) signals weakening real economic activity, which triggers risk-off behavior and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 100.0 (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) combined with stable inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.5%) indicates sustainable demand growth without inflationary pressure, which supports equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in interaction-triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05), or the joint signal fails to achieve Rank IC > 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declines > 0.2pp AND PAYEMS increases > 150k in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both conditions are met (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < -0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% per annum signals a tightening monetary policy regime, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (HOUST) above 1.2 million units per month signals strong housing demand, which drives construction-related corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST > 1200.0 (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
